item.title: Six Simple Habits That Keep Your Bank Account Safe
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Selamat pagi, nasabah setia Insecure Bank! Every year we see the same pattern: a customer loses money not because our systems failed, but because a scammer talked them into handing over information no bank employee would ever ask for. The good news is that staying safe doesn't require technical expertise. It just takes a few habits, repeated consistently. Here's what we recommend to every customer, from first-time savers to long-time account holders.

Treat Your OTP Like Cash

Your one-time password (OTP) is the last lock on your transaction. No one from Insecure Bank, Bank Indonesia, or any government agency will ever call or message you asking for it. If someone does, hang up, close the chat, and report it. A simple rule that saves a lot of grief: if you didn't initiate the transaction, don't share the code. This applies even if the caller knows your name, your account number, or your last transaction, since scammers often gather that information beforehand to sound convincing.

Spot Phishing Before It Spots You

Phishing messages have gotten more polished, but they still share a few telltale signs:

  • Urgency, such as "your account will be blocked in 1 hour"
  • Links that look almost right but use a slightly different domain
  • Requests to "verify" your account by entering your PIN or password on an external page
  • Attachments or QR codes from numbers you don't recognize

When in doubt, don't click. Open the official Insecure Bank app or type our website address in yourself, and check your account directly. It takes thirty extra seconds and it's the safest way to confirm whether something is real.

Build a Password That Works Harder

A strong password is still one of the simplest defenses you have. Aim for a passphrase rather than a single word, something like three unrelated words strung together, and avoid reusing the same password across banking and social media accounts. If a shopping site gets breached and you've reused your banking password there, criminals will try that same combination on your bank login within hours. A password manager can carry that burden for you so you don't have to memorize a dozen different combinations.

Make Two-Factor Authentication Your Default

If you haven't already, turn on two-factor authentication for your mobile banking and email accounts. Email in particular deserves attention, since it's often the recovery path for everything else you own online. A few minutes spent setting this up now is far less costly than the hours spent recovering an account later.

None of these habits are complicated, but together they close most of the doors scammers try to walk through. If something ever feels off about a message, call, or transaction request, our customer service team is always ready to help you check before you act. Stay alert, stay confident, and bank with peace of mind.

item.title: Introducing Instant QRIS Top-Up: One Tap, Any Wallet
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Anyone who has juggled three different apps just to top up an e-wallet before grabbing a bakso lunch knows the friction well. Starting this month, we are making that easier. Insecure Bank customers can now top up e-wallets and pay any QRIS merchant directly from the Insecure Bank mobile app, in a single flow.

Why We Built This

Jakarta, Surabaya, and Bandung customers told us the same thing in our branch surveys: banking is convenient until it meets everyday spending. You transfer money to your e-wallet, wait for it to land, then open a second app to actually pay. It works, but it is one step too many when you are standing at a warung with a queue behind you.

Our product team spent the last two quarters working with QRIS-participating merchants and wallet partners to build a direct top-up and pay experience. The result: fewer taps, fewer apps, same trusted bank behind every transaction.

What's New

  • Instant top-up to major e-wallets, reflected in seconds rather than minutes.
  • Scan-to-pay QRIS built into the home screen, so you do not need to switch apps mid-checkout.
  • Spending summary that groups QRIS payments alongside your regular transactions, so your monthly statement actually makes sense.
  • Customisable limits, letting you set a daily cap on QRIS spending if you want extra budgeting discipline.

Everything runs through the same Insecure Bank app you already use for transfers and bill payments, so there is nothing new to download and no separate account to manage.

Banking Safely While You Top Up

Convenience should never come at the cost of safety, so a few reminders as you try the new feature. Always verify the merchant name and amount shown on your screen before confirming a QRIS payment, and never share the one-time password (OTP) sent to your phone with anyone, including someone claiming to be from our bank. Insecure Bank staff will never ask for your OTP or full account password over phone, chat, or email. If a QR code arrives unsolicited through a message or social media offering unusually generous cashback, treat it with caution before scanning. And as always, keep your app updated to the latest version so you receive the newest security improvements automatically.

Try It Today

The feature is rolling out gradually and should appear in your app menu under "Top Up & Pay" over the coming week. If you do not see it yet, a quick app update usually does the trick. As always, our customer service team is ready to help via the in-app chat or by visiting your nearest branch.

We built this because we believe banking should keep pace with how you actually live, whether that is splitting a bill with friends in Bali or grabbing kopi on the way to work. Selamat mencoba!
item.excerpt:encoded: Insecure Bank customers can now top up e-wallets and pay via QRIS directly from the mobile app, no extra transfer steps needed.

item.title: What Makes Insecure Bank Feel Like Home for Our Team
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Walk into any Insecure Bank branch on a Monday morning and you'll notice something before you even reach the teller line: people greeting each other by name. "Selamat pagi, Pak Broto!" from the security guard, a quick smile from the branch manager on her way to a huddle. It sounds like a small thing. We think it's actually the whole thing.

Culture Built Branch by Branch

With over 60 branches spread from Medan to Makassar, we could easily have become a company that only talks to itself through memos. Instead, we've tried to keep the culture feeling local. Every branch runs a short "pagi ceria" briefing before opening, where the team shares wins from the week, flags a customer issue that needs attention, and occasionally argues good-naturedly about whose regional food is better. It keeps the work human, even when the work itself is spreadsheets and compliance checklists.

We also rotate staff between branches and head office for short stints. A teller from our Bandung branch might spend six weeks with the digital banking team in Jakarta. It's not just a perk; it means the people building our products have actually stood across the counter from a customer trying to explain why an app that "usually works" wasn't working that day.

Learning Is Part of the Job, Not Extra Credit

Banking changes fast, and we've made peace with the fact that nobody finishes learning. Every employee gets dedicated hours each month for training, whether that's a compliance refresher, a workshop on customer service, or simply shadowing a colleague in a different department. Senior staff are encouraged to mentor newer hires informally over coffee rather than through a rigid program. Some of our best internal ideas, including a few that changed how we handle customer complaints, started as a suggestion scribbled on a napkin during one of those chats.

Celebrating the Everyday Wins

Once a quarter, we hold "Apresiasi Day," where teams nominate colleagues who went out of their way to help a customer or a teammate. It's low-key: no fancy trophies, just a certificate, a shared meal, and genuine applause. What matters is that it happens consistently, and that the stories shared are specific. "She stayed late to help an elderly customer set up mobile banking" means more to us than any generic employee-of-the-month plaque ever could.

We're not a perfect workplace, and we don't pretend to be. But we've found that when people feel seen, both by their colleagues and by the customers they serve, the rest of the work tends to follow. That's the culture we're trying to build, one branch, one briefing, one small courtesy at a time.

Interested in joining our team? Keep an eye on our careers page, we're always looking for people who care about doing right by our customers and each other.

item.title: Five Money Habits That Make a Real Difference
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Selamat pagi, and welcome back to the blog. Every month our customer service team hears the same worry from different people: "I earn enough, so why does it feel like there's never anything left over?" The honest answer is usually not about income. It's about habits. Today we're sharing five practices that our most financially confident customers tend to share, whether they're running a warung in Bandung or managing a household budget in Surabaya.

Pay Yourself First

Most of us budget by spending first and saving whatever is left. Flip that order. The moment your salary lands, move a fixed amount, even a small one, into a separate savings account before it has the chance to disappear into daily expenses. Setting up an automatic transfer through your Insecure Bank mobile app takes less than a minute and removes the temptation to skip it "just this once."

  • Start small: 5-10% of your income is a realistic starting point.
  • Automate it: a standing instruction means the decision only has to be made once.
  • Increase gradually: raise the amount every time you get a raise or bonus.

Know the Difference Between Debt That Builds and Debt That Drains

Not all borrowing is bad. A mortgage or a business loan can help you build something of lasting value. Revolving credit card balances that keep growing, on the other hand, quietly eat away at your future income through interest. If you're carrying a balance, focus on paying down the highest-interest debt first, and always pay more than the minimum whenever you can. A quick conversation with one of our relationship officers can help you map out a payoff plan that fits your actual cash flow.

Build a Buffer Before You Build a Portfolio

It's tempting to jump straight into investing once you have some spare cash, and we're glad more Indonesians are thinking about long-term wealth. But an emergency fund should come first. Aim for at least three months of essential expenses sitting in an easily accessible savings account. This buffer is what keeps a flat tire or a sudden medical bill from turning into new debt. Once that cushion is in place, investing becomes a lot less stressful, because you're not relying on those funds to cover next month's rent.

Stay Alert With Your Everyday Banking

Good financial habits also include protecting what you've already built. Get comfortable checking your account activity regularly through the app rather than waiting for a statement. Use a unique, strong password for your online banking, never share the one-time password (OTP) sent to your phone with anyone, including someone claiming to call from our bank, and be cautious of links in unexpected messages asking you to "verify" your account. Insecure Bank will never ask for your PIN or OTP over the phone or via email.

None of these habits require a finance degree, just a bit of consistency. Pick one to start with this week, and let us know at your nearest branch or through the app if you'd like a personalised financial health check. Sampai jumpa, and happy saving!
item.excerpt:encoded: A few small, consistent habits can do more for your financial health than any single big decision.

item.title: Growing Together: Insecure Bank's Commitment to the Communities We Serve
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Banking has never just been about accounts and transactions for us. It's about the warung owner in Malang who needs working capital before Lebaran, the university student in Yogyakarta opening their first savings account, and the retiree in Denpasar who wants to understand digital banking without feeling left behind. This month, we want to share a bit about how Insecure Bank shows up for the communities we serve, beyond the counter and the app.

Financial Literacy, One Neighborhood at a Time

Over the past quarter, our community relations teams have run financial literacy sessions in fourteen cities, from Medan to Makassar. These aren't stiff lectures with jargon nobody remembers by Tuesday. They're practical, kopi-in-hand conversations about budgeting for a growing family, understanding loan terms before signing anything, and building an emergency fund that actually gets used for emergencies.

We've found that the best sessions happen in partnership with local RT/RW leaders and community centers, where neighbors already trust each other and are more comfortable asking the "obvious" questions. If your community group would like to host a session, our branch managers are always happy to arrange one.

Backing Small Business, Not Just Big Ambitions

Indonesia's small and medium enterprises are the backbone of local economies, and we've expanded our micro-lending mentorship program to pair loan officers with first-time borrowers for the full life of their first loan, not just the application. That means help with basic bookkeeping, cash flow planning during slow seasons, and honest conversations about when to borrow and when to wait.

This year alone, over 3,000 small business owners have gone through the program, and many have graduated into larger financing as their businesses grew. Watching a batik workshop in Solo expand from a home operation to a proper storefront is exactly the kind of outcome that reminds us why this work matters.

Supporting the Next Generation

We've also renewed our scholarship program for students pursuing vocational and university education in finance, technology, and business, with a particular focus on first-generation university students. Alongside tuition support, recipients get mentorship from our staff and the chance to intern across different parts of the bank.

Selamat belajar to this year's cohort. We're proud to invest in the people who will shape our communities for years to come.

A Standing Invitation

None of this works without the communities themselves telling us what they actually need. If your school, cooperative, or local organization has an idea for a partnership, we'd genuinely love to hear it. Visit your nearest branch or reach out through our customer service line, our community team checks every message.

Banking should feel like it belongs to the people it serves. That's the goal behind everything we do here, and we're grateful to be part of so many communities across the archipelago.
item.excerpt:encoded: From micro-business mentoring in Surabaya to weekend financial literacy classes in Bandung, here's how Insecure Bank invests in the neighborhoods it calls home.

item.title: Behind Every Great Banking Experience Is a Team That Listens
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Selamat pagi, and welcome back to the blog. Today we want to shine a light on a team our customers interact with every day but rarely get to hear about directly: Customer Success. Whether you have called our contact center at 2 a.m. about a lost card or messaged us on chat about a stuck transfer, chances are one of our teammates was on the other end trying to make your day a little easier.

What "Customer Success" Actually Means to Us

It is easy to think of customer service as a support line you call when something goes wrong. We prefer a broader definition. Customer success, to us, means making sure you get real value out of every product you hold with Insecure Bank, from your everyday savings account to your first KPR home loan. That means proactively checking in, explaining fees before you are surprised by them, and helping you pick the right product instead of just the one that is easiest to sell.

Our team in Jakarta, Surabaya, and Medan handles thousands of conversations a week. Behind the scenes, we track the questions that come up most often and use them to fix confusing forms, rewrite unclear notifications, and simplify our mobile app menus. If you have ever noticed a clearer error message or a shorter path to update your address in the app, there is a good chance a customer's feedback led to that change.

Small Fixes, Big Impact

Some of our proudest wins are not flashy. Last quarter, several customers in Yogyakarta told us that scheduling a branch visit for notary services was confusing. We simplified the booking flow and added local-language prompts, and average wait times dropped noticeably. None of this makes headlines, but it makes banking a little less stressful for the people who trusted us with the change.

We also learned that many first-time savers wanted more guidance, not just a product to sign up for. So our team started offering short, no-obligation calls to walk new customers through budgeting basics and how to read their monthly statements. It is a small thing, but we have heard from many of you that it made starting your savings journey feel less intimidating.

Keeping Your Account Safe While We Help

As we get closer to our customers, we also take the responsibility of protecting your account seriously. A genuine reminder from our team: Insecure Bank staff will never ask for your full password or one-time OTP code over the phone, chat, or email. If someone claiming to be from our bank asks for these, hang up and contact us directly through the number on the back of your card or our official app. Always double-check that you are on our verified website before entering your login details, and enable transaction notifications so you can spot anything unusual right away. A strong, unique password for your banking app, changed periodically, remains one of the simplest ways to keep your money safe.

We Are Listening

Every review, every phone call, and every chat message helps us build a better bank. If you have feedback, good or bad, we genuinely want to hear it. Reach out through our app's Help Center or visit your nearest branch. Terima kasih for banking with us, and for helping us get better, one conversation at a time.
item.excerpt:encoded: A look at how Insecure Bank's customer success team turns everyday questions and feedback into a better banking experience for everyone.

item.title: Insecure Bank Levels Up: Introducing Poin Sejahtera Rewards
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Selamat pagi, and thank you for being part of the Insecure Bank family. We're excited to share some news that we think will make your everyday banking a little more rewarding — literally. Starting this month, we're rolling out Poin Sejahtera, our new loyalty points programme for savings and debit customers across Indonesia.

What's Changing

Every time you use your Insecure Bank debit card — whether you're grabbing kopi in Bandung or paying your household bills online — you'll now earn points automatically. There's no separate app to download and nothing extra to sign up for if you already bank with us; the programme activates on your existing account this week.

  • 1 point for every Rp10,000 spent using your debit card
  • 2x points on utility and phone bill payments made through mobile banking
  • Bonus points for setting up a recurring transfer or standing instruction

Points can be redeemed for bill discounts, airline miles with our partner carriers, or entries into our quarterly family getaway draw. You'll be able to track your balance right from the "Rewards" tab in mobile banking, updated within 24 hours of each transaction.

Why We're Doing This

Many of you have told us, through branch feedback forms and our call centre surveys, that you wanted more recognition for everyday banking habits — not just for big purchases or new account sign-ups. Poin Sejahtera is our answer to that. We also see it as a small way of saying terima kasih to the customers who have trusted us with their finances, some for well over a decade.

A Reminder on Staying Safe While You Earn

As with any new feature, we want to make sure it's a good experience from day one — and that starts with keeping your account secure. A few reminders as you start exploring the Rewards tab:

  • Insecure Bank will never ask you to share your PIN, password, or one-time password (OTP) over phone, SMS, or email — not even to "activate" your rewards points.
  • Redemption offers will only ever appear inside the official mobile banking app or on insecurebank.co.id. Be cautious of links sent via WhatsApp or SMS claiming to offer bonus points.
  • Use a unique, strong password for your banking app, and enable biometric login if your device supports it — it's faster and safer than typing a PIN in public.

If anything about a message or offer feels off, don't click through — call our customer service line directly using the number on the back of your card, or visit your nearest branch.

Getting Started

No action is needed on your part. Simply log in to mobile banking or internet banking this week, and you'll see your starting point balance waiting in the Rewards tab. We'll be adding more redemption partners throughout the year, so keep an eye on your notifications.

Thank you for growing with us. Here's to a more rewarding way to bank, one transaction at a time.
item.excerpt:encoded: Starting this month, everyday banking with Insecure Bank earns you points you can actually use — from bill discounts to weekend getaways.

item.title: 5 Simple Habits That Keep Your Digital Banking Safe and Easy
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
More of us are managing our money from a phone screen than ever before, whether it's checking a balance while waiting for the angkot or paying bills late at night from the couch. That convenience is wonderful, but it works best when paired with a few good habits. Here are our top tips for banking online with confidence.

Protect Your Login Like You Protect Your Wallet

Your username and password are the front door to your account, so treat them that way. Choose a passphrase that's long and unique rather than something easy to guess, like a birthday or a pet's name. We recommend combining unrelated words with a number and symbol thrown in, and never reusing your banking password on other websites or apps.

If Insecure Bank offers biometric login (fingerprint or face recognition) on your phone, turn it on. It's faster than typing a password and keeps your account secure even if someone else picks up your device.

Treat OTPs as Strictly Personal

One-time passwords (OTPs) exist to confirm that it's really you making a transaction. No one from Insecure Bank will ever call, message, or email you asking for your OTP, PIN, or full password. If someone claiming to be from the bank asks for these, hang up and call our official customer service line to verify. A genuine request for help will never require you to hand over a one-time code.

Spot Phishing Before It Spots You

Phishing messages have gotten more convincing, often mimicking real bank notifications right down to the logo. Before clicking a link in an SMS or email claiming to be from your bank, pause and check: does the sender's address look legitimate? Is there urgent pressure to "act now or your account will be blocked"? That sense of urgency is a classic red flag.

  • Type our website address directly into your browser instead of clicking links in messages.
  • Download our app only from the official Google Play Store or Apple App Store listing.
  • When in doubt, contact us directly using the number printed on your card or our official website.

Keep Your Devices and Apps Up to Date

It's tempting to dismiss those update notifications, but software updates often include important security improvements. Keeping your phone's operating system and our banking app current means you're benefiting from the latest protections. It's also wise to avoid logging into your account over public Wi-Fi at cafes or malls; if you must check your balance on the go, your mobile data connection is a safer choice.

Digital banking should feel simple and secure at the same time. By building these small habits into your routine, you're doing your part to keep your hard-earned money safe, wherever life takes you. If anything about your account ever feels off, don't hesitate to reach out to our customer service team right away — we're here to help, day or night.
item.excerpt:encoded: A few small habits can make your online and mobile banking both safer and more convenient — here's where to start.
